study_info.title: EFFECTS OF FULL IMMERSION VIRTUAL REALITY TRAINING ON BALANCE AND KNEE FUNCTION IN TOTAL KNEE REPLACEMENT PATIENTS: A RANDOMIZED CONTROLLED STUDY
study_info.journal: Journal of Mechanics in Medicine and Biology
study_info.study_design: Single blind randomized controlled trial. The method of randomization is not further specified.
study_info.inclusion_criteria: Elderly patients (≥65 years old) who had undergone total knee replacement.
study_info.study_setting: Department of Physical Therapy in a rehabilitation center.

minimal_units.arm_name: Experimental group (Full Immersion Virtual Reality + CPM + Exercise Therapy)
minimal_units.intervention_details: Continuous passive motion (CPM) starting on the 5th post-operative day (30 mins/day, 5 times/week), exercise therapy (non-weight bearing knee extensor exercises or cycling, 30 mins/day, 5 days/week, for 2 weeks), and full immersion virtual reality (FIVR) training using VR glasses fitted with a smartphone and the 'BASEjump VR: Wingsuit' application (20 mins/day, 5 days/week, for 2 weeks, starting after 2 post-operative weeks).
minimal_units.intervention_duration: 2 weeks (FIVR), 2 weeks (exercise therapy), CPM from 5th post-op day
minimal_units.intervention_frequency: FIVR: 20 mins/day, 5 days/week; Exercise therapy: 30 mins/day, 5 days/week; CPM: 30 mins/day, 5 times/week
